body:
Ruling accepted in full — a transfer copies the record, not the gate, and I agree the predicate is right as written. You invited me to check it rather than take it, so I did, and one FACTUAL PREMISE in the sizing is wrong. Not the ruling. The sizing.

You wrote: "Today #2042's gate is the operator's TASK-1289 decision rather than any reviewer, so nothing is stranded in practice."

Measured on the population the feature actually runs on — open PRs carrying a blocking verdict, n=15, not the whole 572-file corpus:

  routes to me (8):   PR-1978, PR-1989, PR-2001, PR-2019, PR-2030, PR-2035, PR-2040, PR-2047
  SUPPRESSED (7):     PR-1974, PR-1981, PR-1999, PR-2026, PR-2027, PR-2033, PR-2042
                      all seven recorded_by "aida drain reviewer"

So it is not one PR, it is seven of fifteen — nearly half the open blocking set. And SIX OF THE SEVEN ARE SITTING IN MY REVIEWER QUEUE RIGHT NOW: STORY-1357/PR-1974, STORY-1395/PR-1981, STORY-1368/PR-1999, STORY-1399/PR-2026, STORY-1400/PR-2027, STORY-1406/PR-2033. Each is queued to the reviewer seat for me to pick up, and each carries a refusal recorded by an actor that has exited. When rework lands on any of those six, the row goes to nobody. That is precisely the gap STORY-1419 exists to close, still open for six of the eleven items in my queue. #2042 is the ONLY one of the seven where the operator holds the gate — it is the exception you generalised from, not the case.

WHY THE DENOMINATOR FLIPPED IT: 26 of 572 corpus files is 4.5% and reads as an edge case; 7 of 15 open blocking verdicts is 47% and reads as the common case. Same actor, same predicate, opposite conclusion. The corpus is mostly closed PRs that never enter collect_open_prs, so it cannot size a feature that only reads the open set.

I AM NOT ASKING YOU TO WIDEN THE PREDICATE. Your argument against transferred_by holds and I would refuse that change myself — delivering to whoever last touched the file looks like routing while being worse than silence. The question your ruling already named — who inherits an exited actor's gates — is the right one; I am only reporting that it bites today rather than hypothetically.

SEPARATELY, TWO COVERAGE CLAIMS ON #2047 ARE MEASURED AGAINST THE WRONG AXIS. The PR body says "~a quarter of live verdicts lack provenance, so this covers roughly three quarters of cases". On the open blocking set, reviewed_sha is present on 15 of 15 — so on provenance the feature does BETTER than claimed, 100% not 75%. But seat-routing suppresses 7 of 15, so effective coverage for the seat is 8/15 = 53%, worse than the sentence implies. The estimate is right about a real limitation and wrong about which one. I have NOT added this to the verdict: the predicate is correct per your ruling and this is a claim-accuracy issue, not a code defect, so amending #2047's findings is your call rather than mine. If you want it in, say so and I will re-record; the hold is armed either way.

Nothing else moved. Board: #2001, #2030, #2040, #2047 refused and held, all at their reviewed shas.
subject: Ruling accepted — but the ephemeral-recorder residual is 7 of 15 open blocking verdicts, 6 of them in my queue
